role: startup co-founder (positioning, objections, pricing, conversion path, truthfulness)
verdict: The page sells one sharp promise (your first line, your facts, your voice), proves it with a working demo inside two scrolls, prices it exactly and honestly, and never claims anything the preview cannot back up. I found no P0 or P1 at 1440 or 390; what is left is small polish on demo depth and one pricing ambiguity.

issues.where: Try box result, own line: "honestly i dont know if anyone needs to hear this but stop averaging down on losers"
issues.problem: The on-device check cuts only "honestly" and says "the claim stands on its own", while the line still opens on "i dont know if anyone needs to hear this but", one of the most common throat-clearing openers on X. A creator will spot that the bigger fluff survived at the exact moment they decide whether to sign up. Same family: "Here are 7 lessons I learned from" returns Nothing to cut, and a trailing "actually" is kept.
issues.fix: Add the stock X run-ups ("i don't know who/if anyone needs to hear this but", "here are N lessons I learned from", trailing "actually"/"tbh") to the on-device rules as cuts or 'your call' marks, so the result opens on "stop averaging down on losers". Until then, do not show the 'claim stands on its own' reason when a hedge clause still leads the line.

issues.where: Studio card: "Up to 8 client voices. Yours is included."
issues.problem: A ghostwriter cannot tell whether their own voice is a free extra or one of the eight billed at $18. That is the first sum an agency does before buying.
issues.fix: Say it outright, in the same line length, e.g. "Up to 8 client voices. Your own is free." (or "Your own counts as one" if that is the truth).

issues.where: Phone pricing, Free card (two bullets visible)
issues.problem: On a phone the Free card shows only Sharpen and 15 scheduled posts; the strongest free hooks (learns your voice from 8 posts, 20 rewrites) sit behind 'See everything included', so Free reads thinner than it is next to the headline 'Sharpening is free. Forever.'
issues.fix: Swap the second visible bullet's sub-clause for one short line, e.g. "15 scheduled posts and 20 rewrites a month", mirroring Pro's combined '500 posts and 250 rewrites a month' bullet. No added height.

issues.where: Try box when nothing is cut (e.g. "We shipped v2.0 today.")
issues.problem: The primary button becomes 'Schedule it free' while the more persuasive next step (three rewrites in your voice) is only a text link in the sentence above. For a visitor whose line was already clean, the rewrite is the reason to sign up, not scheduling.
issues.fix: Keep the copy, but make the pill 'Get three takes, free' and demote 'Schedule it free' to the text link; both open the same sheet with the line carried over.

issues.problem: The answer is good but long for the objection most paying prospects arrive with; the key sentence ('Sharpen is free, whatever you post with') is followed by three sentences about imports before the reader gets the reason to switch.
issues.fix: Cut to three sentences: keep it and use Sharpen free; or bring your posts (Typefully or CSV export, X archive); they are read in your browser and teach it how you open and when your people reply.
